transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-07-29 15:00 UTC
Duration: 49 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Priya Natarajan (Ashgrove Cloud Architect), Ethan Cole (Ashgrove Security Lead), Maya Lin (Ashgrove Platform Eng)

Auto-summary (AI generated): Quick discovery call focused on private/on-prem connectivity. Customer requires region-locked processing for PHI, wants options for on-prem bridge and private endpoints. Discussion covered transit gateway vs peering, egress controls and KMS integration. Several follow-ups agreed.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Lena): "hey everyone, thanks for joining on short notice. can you all do quick intros? we'll keep this to 45, 50 minutes tops, try to capture action items"
00:07 Speaker 2 (Priya): "hi, i'm priya, cloud architect at ashgrove, i manage the vpc designs and regulatory constraints for our clinical data pipelines"
00:15 Speaker 3 (Ethan): "ethan, security lead, focused on encryption, audit logs, and least-privilege networking"
00:22 Speaker 4 (Maya): "maya, platform eng, i'll be the day-to-day for integration and ci/cd"
00:30 Speaker 1 (Lena): "great, marco will lead the technical part, i'll help on procurement/pricing and followups"

01:02 Marco (SE): "cool, maybe i'll start with our deployment modes very quickly — hosted api is simplest but we know you have region-lock and on-prem requirements; dedicated is reserved gpu pools in our clouds, private is where we ship a customer-controlled control plane and private dataplane (vpc/private endpoints or on-prem gateway). any particular constraints we should call out up front?"
01:18 Priya: "yes — primary: patient data must not leave EU-2 region. we also have some legacy inference on an onprem cluster at our data center in munich, we need either direct connectivity to that, or a way to run inference there. latency for live triage is around 150ms SLA from clinician app to model, ideally <200ms. also we use cross-account peering and transit gateway at the moment for other services"
01:35 Marco: "okay that's helpful — couple clarifying q's: when you say \"onprem cluster\" is it air-gapped? do you have direct connect or vpn today?"
01:44 Priya: "not air gapped, but restricted; we have an aws direct connect into our colo and some customers are behind a private mpls — typical enterprise setup"
01:53 Ethan: "we also have a very strict egress policy — anything leaving the vpc must go through our egress proxy and get inspected; outbound to public internet is heavily restricted. we cannot have tokens or PHI stored in third-party logs. we need KMS integration so keys never leave our control"
02:08 Marco: "right — so two main patterns we typically propose: 1) private endpoints + VPC peering (or privatelink/privatelink equivalent) from your VPC into our private service endpoints in the same cloud region, or 2) run the inference dataplane on-prem via our on-prem gateway/appliance and keep everything behind your network. each has tradeoffs for latency and ops. for direct connect you'd probably prefer option 2 for strict control"
02:25 Maya: "how does the on-prem gateway work? is it an appliance, a container, do we need special hardware?"
02:31 Marco: "it's containerized but we package it with a small runtime and a secure tunnel to the Redwood control plane; you can run it behind your firewall. we also support an air-gapped package for very high reg cases but that is heavier. in your case, since you have direct connect, we can peer over a private path — that keeps traffic inside datacenter to our inference runtime if you choose the hybrid dataplane"
02:48 Ethan: "what about audit logs and key management? does the gateway call into your control plane? we need assurance that no PHI is logged outside"
02:55 Marco: "good q — we support customer-managed KMS; for private deployments the customer supplies key material via KMS/HSM integration and logs are scrubbed of PHI by default. we can disable telemetry that includes tokens, and we provide an audit-log forwarding option into your SIEM over a private channel"
03:10 Priya: "we also need region gating — even within EU we have to keep compute in eu-west-3 only. can we pin to a specific availability zone/region?"
03:18 Marco: "yes, for private and dedicated customers you can pin model execution to a region. our hosted API is multiregion but not suitable for your constraints. dedicated pools can be allocated in a region and private on-prem obviously runs where you put it"
03:31 Lena: "quick note on pricing tradeoffs: dedicated reserved capacity has predictable sku pricing, on-prem has a licensing and support overlay. we'll put numbers on this in the follow-up"

04:05 Speaker 2 (Priya): "so stepping back — we have three goals: 1) make sure PHI never crosses region boundaries, 2) low latency for clinician-facing requests, 3) minimal operational overhead for platform team. does that align with what you saw?"
04:12 Marco: "yep that tracks. we usually propose an architecture doc + networking checklist. can i walk through a couple of concrete topologies?"
04:19 Priya: "please"

04:30 Marco: "Topology A: in-cloud private endpoints. You create a VPC in eu-west-3, we create private endpoints (privatelink-style) in that region, you peer your app VPC to the endpoint VPC or use the privatelink; ingress and egress stay in-region, and latency is typically sub-50ms within region. downside: data goes to our managed dataplane even though isolated to region — you need to be comfortable with our private tenancy and shared control plane"
05:00 Priya: "we try to avoid third-party control planes if it touches raw PHI — how separated is the control plane?"
05:06 Marco: "control plane is separate from the dataplane; for Private deployments the control plane can be customer-owned or a thin control plane we host and you manage network access to. dataplane can be customer-hosted. we can also support hybrid: control plane hosted, dataplane in your VPC"
05:21 Ethan: "is there a path where we keep keys in our HSM and the model never sees plaintext data?"
05:27 Marco: "we support envelope encryption with customer KMS; the HSM holds key material and the runtime only sees decrypted blobs in memory for the minimal processing window. we also offer techniques for token redaction in logs"

05:58 Maya: "Topology B: on-prem gateway. You run the inference runtime in our container on a host inside our colo. The host talks to your app over private peering/direct connect; we can enforce that no telemetry leaves your network. This gives you full data residency and low latency but is more ops heavy for you"
06:20 Priya: "do you support autoscaling for on-prem? we may have burst demands"
06:25 Marco: "we can provide a hybrid autoscaling where a local pool handles steady state and you burst to our dedicated cloud pool in the same region if you allow limited egress; otherwise you'd need to provision for peak on-prem"
06:36 Ethan: "bursting to cloud is a non-starter unless we have a strict egress inspection and tokenization step — we need to approve any burst flows"
06:45 Marco: "understood, that can be integrated with your egress proxy to enforce inspection and we can only burst encrypted payloads with egress rules"

07:05 Speaker 1 (Lena): "Priya, can you share your current CIDRs and whether you use TGW (transit gateway) or peering for cross-account traffic? that will help narrow the diagram"
07:14 Priya: "we use a central transit gateway and have overlapping 10.0 ranges in some dev accounts, production is clean. CIDR for prod app VPC is 10.8.0.0/16. we also have a colo with an on-prem block 172.16.0.0/20"
07:30 Marco: "great — we need that detail plus egress proxy address and any forced-tunnel configs"

08:02 Ethan: "one more question on private endpoints: if you give us an endpoint in our account, does your service have cross-account roles or do we run instances in our account?"
08:11 Marco: "two models: privatelink style (we create an endpoint service and you create the interface endpoint in your account) or we run your dataplane nodes as instances you control in your account for Dedicated/Private. privatelink is lower ops but still involves some service side component"
08:25 Maya: "what about IP management? we have limited /24s for endpoints"
08:30 Marco: "we can use ENIs or hostnetwork configs to minimize IP usage; we'll include IP planning in the checklist"

09:00 Priya: "how do you handle software updates for the on-prem runtime? we need strict change control"
09:07 Marco: "we ship signed updates, you can opt into automatic patching or schedule manual rollouts. for highly regulated environments, we do a staged release and provide the exact binary hashes"
09:18 Ethan: "can you integrate with our SIEM for audit logs and send them over a private forwarder? we can't send logs to a public bucket"
09:24 Marco: "yes, we support syslog/forwarders over private links and can push to your SIEM endpoint over the direct connect"

10:02 Priya: "latency numbers: if we run onprem, we'd expect 20-40ms roundtrip in colo to app; private endpoints in region ~40-80ms; hosted outside region >200ms which is unacceptable"
10:14 Marco: "that matches our benchmarks; i'll send the spreadsheets but note that latency depends on model size and KV cache warmup — we'll include that in the workshop"

11:05 Speaker 2 (Priya): "one operational constraint: our legal team requires proof that log retention is configurable and that no debug dumps containing PHI will be transmitted without encryption and approvals"
11:13 Marco: "we can set log retention windows and obfuscation rules per customer; we also have a \"no debug dumps\" policy for private deployments unless explicitly enabled"
11:20 Lena: "we'll add log retention config and sample retention policy to the docs pack"

12:00 Maya: "are there known pitfalls with transit gateway and privatelink combos? we've run into route table complexity before"
12:07 Marco: "yeah route table complexity and overlapping cidrs are the main pain points; another gotcha is MTU on some direct connect circuits — we have a troubleshooting checklist for that"
12:15 Priya: "would you ever recommend NATting endpoints? we try to avoid that"
12:20 Marco: "prefer not to NAT; better to use interface endpoints or host-managed nodes so we don't mess with your NAT rules"

13:05 Ethan: "compliance: can you provide a bake-off report or a whitepaper showing how data flows are audited and keys managed?"
13:13 Lena: "yes, we'll share SOC2 plus our private deployment security pack and a short whitepaper on KMS/HSM integration — marco will include flow diagrams"

14:00 Marco: "quick demo note — for the architecture workshop i propose we run two scenarios: 1) private endpoints with strict egress inspection and 2) full onprem gateway with burst-to-dedicated disabled. we'll bring a network person and security SME"
14:15 Priya: "sounds good, propose times and we'll get our networking folks on"

14:40 Speaker 3 (Ethan): "one tiny detail — we use SAML/SSO and prefer identity brokering with minimal access. can you support SCIM + SSO for user provisioning and RBAC?"
14:50 Marco: "yes, we support SSO (SAML/OIDC), SCIM, and fine-grained RBAC in the console. for private deployments we can federate against your IdP"

15:25 Maya: "we have a few large models; does Redwood support mixed-precision quantization on-prem to reduce memory?"
15:32 Marco: "yes, our runtime supports quantization and we can recommend profiles per workload — optimize for throughput/latency tradeoff"

16:00 Priya: "ok recapping next steps — you will: send a network checklist, sample topology diagrams, security pack and pricing; we will: share CIDRs, egress proxy details, and confirm availability for a 60m workshop"
16:14 Lena: "yep that's the plan. i'll schedule the workshop and include marco and our solutions architect"
16:22 Marco: "i'll start the diagrams and include two topologies and an IP plan. i'll also include a note on KMS/HSM integration options"

16:45 Speaker 2 (Priya): "thanks, appreciate the clarity — we'll aim to have our network person join the workshop; tentative date suggests 2027-08-04 but we'll confirm"
16:52 Speaker 1 (Lena): "great, we'll follow up with the doc pack and a calendared workshop invite. any last questions?"
16:58 Maya: "nope all good from me"
17:02 Ethan: "one last ask — can you include an example runbook for incident response if the inference service is unreachable?"
17:09 Marco: "yes, i'll add a runbook + playbook to the materials"
17:20 Lena: "thanks everyone, speak soon"

End of transcript.

Notes / imperfections: occasional mis-heard acronyms (we recorded "smell" instead of SAML), some speaker labels generic, timestamps approximate.
